claims.statement: agent/dashboard/options.py is the single registry of selectable models: SUPPORTED_MODELS is a hand-maintained list of ModelOption records (provider-prefixed id, label, per-model efforts list, default_effort, supports_images), and SUPPORTED_MODEL_IDS is the frozen set every resolution layer checks membership against.

The efforts a model accepts are per-model and non-uniform (e.g. Kimi K3 only accepts low/high/max, some models omit none, only some advertise xhigh/max), and model_supports_effort/model_supports_images validate a stored selection against the model's own ModelOption fields.

Deprecated model ids are not canonically replaced: DEPRECATED_MODEL_REPLACEMENTS has empty values and canonical_model_pair always returns None. Deprecated ids are excluded from provider_fallback_pair and defer to defaults, while unsupported non-deprecated ids may use same-provider and, where possible, same-Claude-family fallback.

default_model_pair() is the deployment-level terminal fallback: it reads LLM_MODEL_ID and LLM_REASONING_EFFORT, validates that the resulting model is supported and default-eligible, and raises ValueError for an unsupported model or effort.

For a hosted agent run, the factory seeds team main/subagent defaults, applies a profile only when no stored thread model exists, then uses stored thread settings when present; a valid explicit configurable agent_model_id/agent_effort is the mechanism that replaces that snapshot and the resolved settings are persisted back to the thread.

agent_overrides.resolve_agent_model_id resolves a supported per-thread id over a valid profile override over the team default, while dashboard thread_api._resolve_agent_model_choice resolves a valid request pair over profile over team default and leaves the team default for a deprecated request.

Every team-default resolution routes candidates through _resolve_default_pair, which returns the pair if supported, else the same-provider fallback, else the global default, guaranteeing the factory ends with a valid constructible pair even when the store is stale or a selection is unknown.

Team defaults are stored as a single LangGraph Store record keyed 'default' in the ['team_settings'] namespace, and get_team_settings merges the stored record over hardcoded defaults fail-soft so an unreachable store degrades to defaults rather than failing every run.

get_team_default_model resolves distinct defaults per role (agent/reviewer/chat), where the chat role inherits the team agent default when no chat-specific model is configured, and separate resolvers exist for the diff-grouping pass (inheriting reviewer subagent) and the thread-title model.

Per-user profiles live in the ['profiles'] namespace holding default_model, reasoning_effort, an optional subagent pair, repository/branch and PR preferences; profile-editable settings are deliberately split from the encrypted GitHub OAuth token stored in ['oauth_tokens'] so a profile save and a concurrent login/refresh cannot clobber each other's fields.

On the run-start path profiles are read fail-soft (agent_overrides.load_profile logs and returns None so a store blip costs only per-user overrides), whereas dashboard reads use profiles.get_profile so failures surface.

normalize_profile_overrides accepts a profile's (default_model, reasoning_effort) only when both are valid, otherwise falls back to the same-provider pair for an unsupported id, and returns (None, None) for an absent/unknown-provider selection so the team default applies.

provider_model_kwargs translates a resolved effort string into provider-specific kwargs by dispatching on the model id prefix: OpenAI gets a reasoning dict (summary auto for non-none efforts), Anthropic gets adaptive/summarized thinking plus an effort field, Gemini 3+ gets thinking_level, Fireworks gets model_kwargs.reasoning_effort, and Baseten gets reasoning_effort for low/high/max.

make_model builds a chat model via init_chat_model and applies a default max_retries of 6 and a 600s per-request timeout for known provider prefixes so a stalled provider connection becomes a retry instead of a wedged run.

make_model configures OpenAI models for the Responses API with store=false, output_version responses/v1, and include reasoning.encrypted_content, and uses desktop OpenAI OAuth when no OPENAI_API_KEY is set and the gateway is not applied.
make_model routes Baseten as an OpenAI-compatible provider and, when the gateway is disabled, requires BASETEN_API_KEY and points at the Baseten base URL, raising if the key is missing.

The dashboard /options response enriches copies of selectable ModelOption records with context-window values from Codex overrides, LangChain provider profiles, or fallbacks; make_model injects an override profile for configured Codex context-window variants and caches constructed models keyed on model id, gateway argument, max tokens, frozen kwargs, and event-loop id, with close_cached_models tearing them down.

Gateway routing is tri-state: resolve_gateway_enabled treats a team gateway_enabled of True/False as authoritative and None as inheriting the LANGSMITH_GATEWAY_ENABLED deployment default (gateway_env_default), and when enabled gateway_overrides supplies base_url/api_key/use_responses_api that override direct-provider defaults.

fallback_model_id_for returns a cross-provider fallback (Anthropic primaries -> OpenAI and vice versa) and None for Google/local/self-hosted providers that must not be silently re-routed; the run factory wires this into ModelFallbackMiddleware honoring an LLM_FALLBACK_MODEL_ID env override first.

Fable (ZDR) models are gated workspace-wide: gate_fable_model swaps a resolved Fable id for a safe non-Fable Anthropic model whenever fable_enabled is false, and the factory gates main, subagent, and title models while the dashboard resolver and options response gate selections, preventing disabled Fable from being constructed or advertised.

Per-repo custom instructions are admin-authored records stored in the ['agent_instructions'] namespace keyed by owner/name; the run factory resolves them via get_repo_agent_instructions and renders them into the system prompt as 'Repository-specific Custom Instructions', so they apply to the whole thread.

Per-user custom instructions live in their own ['user_instructions'] namespace keyed by GitHub login (capped at 20,000 chars) precisely because they can be written both from the dashboard Profile tab and by the agent's save_user_instructions tool, so the two writers do not clobber each other.

Per-user instructions are attached to the triggering user's message via construct_sender_context and rendered by _render_user_instructions_section as sender-level standing instructions scoped to only the current turn, distinct from the repo instructions embedded in the shared system prompt.

Instruction conflicts resolve in a strict order AGENTS.md > repository custom instructions > user-level (sender) instructions: the prompt tells the agent AGENTS.md overrides defaults with prompt-level authority, repo instructions yield to AGENTS.md, and user-level instructions yield to both repo instructions and AGENTS.md.
For dashboard image-bearing run creation, a text-only resolved model is replaced with default_vision_model_pair; direct image-content validation rejects a missing or text-only model with HTTP 422.

Thread settings are a cached agent_settings metadata snapshot that strips legacy participant-specific fields; failed loads return an empty snapshot and failed writes are logged without aborting a run.
